positions.label: flush with the front and rear panels
positions.name: flush

ac.description: The base switch with two AC supplies and four fans, front-to-rear air: DCS-7280DR3A-36-F ("2 x AC"). Spares: PWR-2411-AC-RED, FAN-7012H-RED.

ac-k.description: The DR3AK-36 with large routes and TunnelSec: DCS-7280DR3AK-36-F, the same face, supplies and fans as the base switch. Table 4 gives it the base switch's power draw.

ac-k-s.description: The DR3AK-36 with secure boot enabled: DCS-7280DR3AK-36S-F ("large routes and TunnelSec, front to rear air, 2 x AC, secure boot enabled"), the same face, supplies and fans as the K.

ac-m.description: The DR3AM-36 with TunnelSec: DCS-7280DR3AM-36-F, the same face, supplies and fans as the base switch. Table 4 gives it the base switch's power draw.

base.description: The chassis as it ships: two AC supplies and four fans in, all thirty-six QSFP-DD and both OSFP cages empty. The orderable builds below are this chassis with a licence and encryption variant.

dc.description: Two DC supplies in place of the AC ones, front-to-rear air: what a "DCS-7280DR3A-36#" order (configurable fans and psu) with PWR-2411-DC-RED gives. The data sheet lists no DC part number of its own, so this is a worked build and not an orderable one.

datasheet.title: 7280R3A Series Data Center Switch Router - Data Sheet (04-0040-26, April 15th, 2025)

description: Arista 7280DR3A-36 - a fixed 2RU data-centre router switch with 36 400G QSFP-DD ports in two stacked rows of eighteen columns (the odd number on the upper cage), numbered 1 to 36 in an orange strip between the rows, and two OSFP line-system ports (OSFP-LS, 37 and 38) for 400G-ZR optics at the upper right. Beside the line-system ports are four status lamps (system, fan, power supply 1, power supply 2), an RJ-45 console, a USB port and an RJ-45 management port; at the far right stand a Time-of-Day connector (USB-C) and two clock connectors (1PPS and 10 MHz). The rear carries four hot-swap fan modules and two hot-swap 2400 W power supplies, AC or DC, one above the other at the right, with a grounding pad between fans 1 and 2. The same front panel is sold as the DR3A-36, the DR3AM-36 (TunnelSec) and the DR3AK-36 (large routes and TunnelSec), and the DR3AK-36S (the K with secure boot enabled); they differ in software licence, encryption and secure boot, not in the metal.

gaps.wanted: A FIGURE OF THE DR3A-36 AND THE DR3AK-36 FRONT. Figure C-2 is captioned for all three models but prints the plate "7280DR3AM-36", so it is a picture of the DR3AM-36. The model plate of the other two is not shown, and this file prints "7280DR3A-36" on every configuration. A photograph of each plate closes it.

THE WHITE NUMBER TABS OVER THE CAGES. Figure C-2 draws a white square with a large numeral over the centre of each cage. A seated cage hides what is painted under it and the library has no layer above a cage for printed matter, so the numbers are modelled as the strip legends only. A drawing that says whether the tab is a sticker on the cage or part of it closes it.

A LEGEND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE FIRST STRIP. Column 1's strip reads something like "400G" between its arrows in the eight-times enlargement and no other column's does. At 1.87 px/mm the glyphs are three pixels high and resolve to a smear; the numerals and arrows beside it resolve, so the strip is readable and this text is the unresolved thing. It is not drawn.

THE SYMBOLS OVER THE SYSTEM AND FAN LAMPS, and the small legends over the console and management jacks. They are printed in blue at about two pixels' height and are not legible in the figure; PS1 and PS2 are. Guide figures A-1 and A-2 say the lamps are labelled in one of two ways and the held figure does not say which this chassis uses.
A LAMP AND A BLUE SYMBOL ABOVE THE ToD CONNECTOR (about 428.9 and 434.8 mm, 34.3 mm down). Figure C-2 draws them and no callout or table names them. They are not modelled.

WHETHER THE PPS AND 10MHZ JACKS ARE SMB OR SMA. The guide calls them "E-Sync clock connectors" and the data sheet "PPS/10M/ToD inputs"; neither names the connector. They are seated as std/smb@1 from their drawn size and their direction (input or output) is not stated either.

THE USB GENERATION. The guide says "USB port" and the data sheet "USB Ports 1"; neither gives a generation, and figure C-2 draws a gold tongue, which is neither USB-IF colour. The port is seated with the `usb2` (white) skin as the one that claims least; a data sheet line giving the generation closes it.

A BLACK ROUND HOLE at the left end, 4.8 mm from the edge and 53.4 mm down, in line with the strips. Figure C-2 draws it and nothing names it (an ESD socket is a candidate on other switches). It is drawn as a hole in decor and carries no part.

THE PRINTING AT THE REAR. The ground strip prints three symbols and the rear carries the airflow marks, but the guide's rear panel figure is 1.19 px/mm and its labels are unreadable. The supplies and fans print no numbers that resolve. A rear photograph closes it.

THE PWR-2411-DC FACE. The guide shows the PWR-1900-DC and PWR-500-DC (figure 4-5) and no PWR-2411-DC. Table 7 note 2 says its terminals are "twin #10 studs spaced for dual-hole lug with 5/8 inch hole spacing"; the supply here is the AC housing with a plain two-pole block, and the protective earth terminal "on the opposite side" is not drawn. The data sheet reads "AWG #6 Max" for the DC input connector and table 7 reads 2 to 4 AWG; the larger conductor (the guide's) is the one a lug takes.

THE KITS, AND THE EAR POSITION THAT IS NOT FLUSH. `chassis.ears` states the one position the guide names for a 2RU switch: section 3.5 says the bracket sits "either flush with the front and rear panels, or not flush with the panels", and section 3.4 gives no two-post mounting for the 2RU switches, so the position is `4-post` only. It has no `at` (the guide's mounting figures are isometric drawings of other switches, the 7050 and the 7050SX-128), no `default` (no figure shows the ears as shipped) and the "not flush" case is left out because the guide does not say which way it sits. The data sheet's ordering information lists KIT-7202 (spare tool-free accessory kit v2 for 2RU, 4-post mount, 2x C19-C20) and KIT-7004-2UL (extended tool-free 4-post kit for 2-4RU) for the DR3A-36. Guide appendix B.1 gives KIT-7202 "rack depths of twenty two to thirty two inches" (558.8 to 812.8 mm) and its parts (ASY-06132 rack ear, ASY-03765 front rail, ASY-03767 rear sliding rail, two of each), but no document dimensions any of those parts, and none gives KIT-7004-2UL a range or a parts list. A kit contract needs its parts as components with a size, so neither kit is modelled and `chassis.kits` is left out.
THE POWER DRAW OF FAN-7012H. Neither the guide nor the data sheet gives it. The supplies' own output (2400 W) is stated and is written.
The K and M variants print their own model line on the plate. This file prints one line.

mgmt.mixed: the machine's management interfaces: an RJ-45 serial console, a USB port for software and configuration updates, and a 10/100/1000 RJ-45 Ethernet management port, in a row at the upper right (guide section 4.5: "For most models, the front panel contains the console, management, and USB ports").

osfp-ls-400g.description: the two OSFP line-system ports, printed 37 and 38 (their ids are port-37 and port-38) and counted 1 and 2 here as the guide's callout table does ("Line system port (OSFP)" 1 and 2), beside the status lamps. The data sheet calls them OSFP-LS and says they are for dense 400G-ZR deployment.

attrs.redundancy-note: datasheet: "Hot-swap Power Supplies 2 (1+1 redundant)"; guide section 4.4: "The switch operates with two installed power supplies. At least one power supply must connect to a power source."

qsfpdd-400g.description: the thirty-six 400G QSFP-DD ports in EIGHTEEN COLUMNS OF TWO on a 23.05 mm pitch, numbered 1 to 36 down each column from 1 at the top left, with `N up-arrow` and `down-arrow N+1` printed in the orange strip between the two cages of each column.

timing.mixed: the precision-timing connectors at the right edge: a Time-of-Day connector (USB-C, the mate of CAB-SYNCE-RJ) and two coax clock connectors, 1PPS and 10MHz, which the guide calls "E-Sync clock connectors". The data sheet's "PPS/10M/ToD inputs".

name: 7280dr3a-36

configurations.note: FOUR ORDERABLE CONFIGURATIONS OF ONE FACE. The data sheet's ordering information for the 7280DR3A-36 lists DCS-7280DR3A-36-F ("front to rear air, 2 x AC"), DCS-7280DR3AM-36-F ("TunnelSec"), DCS-7280DR3AK-36-F ("large routes and TunnelSec") and DCS-7280DR3AK-36S-F ("large routes and TunnelSec, secure boot enabled"), and the same four ending "#" ("configurable fans and psu"). The F orders are the only part numbers with a fixed build, so they are the orderable configurations. The "#" orders take their supplies and fans to order, which is how a DC build is bought (PWR-2411-DC-RED is a listed spare and table 4 lists PWR-2411-DC); there is no DC part number, so the DC build is a `kind: example` configuration, shown but not exported. Table 4 of the guide gives one figure (643 W typical, 1283 W maximum) for the DR3A-36, DR3AM-36 and DR3AK-36, so no configuration states a power of its own. The guide's Table 1 gives all three one size and weight; the data sheet's model comparison table differs only in the Encryption row (none, all ports, all ports).

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, 0 to 3,000 m, 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. The data sheet's environmental table gives the same operating and altitude figures and humidity, and a storage range of -40 to 70 C. The guide (the newer, 2025-05-16 against 2025-04-15) is used for storage; the data sheet's is in `other` as written.

field-replaceable-units.note: EVERY FAN MODULE AND POWER SUPPLY IS A BAY. The guide's appendix E: "All fans and power supplies are hot swappable" and "all slots must be filled or covered with a blank for operation". The data sheet's comparison table: "Hot-swap Power Supplies 2 (1+1 redundant)", "Hot-swappable Fans 4 (N+1 redundant)", "Fan Tray FAN-7012H" and "Power Supplies PWR-2411 (AC or DC)". Nothing in the held documents draws a blank for either bay, so none is modelled. The supply and fan the DR3A-36 takes are front-to-rear (red) only: the data sheet lists "Airflow Direction: Front to Rear" and only the RED spares (PWR-2411-AC-RED, PWR-2411-DC-RED, FAN-7012H-RED). The guide's section 2.1 says a red handle is an air-exit module and a blue one an air-inlet module, so this switch is wholly red and has no airflow configuration.

gate-1.note: Figure C-2 is a 872 x 344 px raster (PDF image, 129 ppi). The chassis in it spans 823 px (x 2 to 825) and 161 px (y 105 to 266, with a ribbed lower lip) - aspect 5.12, against 5.005 for the data sheet's 43.99 x 8.79 cm body (4.4 percent out) and 5.49 for a 48.3 cm face over the ears, so the figure shows the body with no ears. 4.4 percent is at the edge of what the method allows. THE X AXIS IS TAKEN (1.873 px/mm on the 440 mm body) AND THE Y AXIS IS THE SAME SCALE, not its own: the row pitch measured 26.5 px is 14.15 mm on the x scale against 14.2 to 14.3 for stacked QSFP-DD cages elsewhere in the library, while the y scale (1.832 px/mm) would make it 14.5. The figure is cut about 2 mm short at the bottom. Every front position below is therefore a reading good to about one pixel, 0.55 mm, and is estimated. The rear figure D-3 is a 565 x 197 px raster whose chassis is 525 px (x 2 to 527) by 105.5 px (y 47 to 152.5): aspect 4.98 against 5.005, 0.6 percent out, so it passes, at 1.193 px/mm. One pixel is 0.84 mm there.

ground-pad.note: A grey strip 15.0 mm wide between fans 1 and 2 (x 87.2 to 102.2) holds two black holes 19.2 mm apart (y 13.0 and 32.2), a ground symbol between them and, below, three printed symbols (a warning triangle, a box, a person-and-bar) too small to read. The holes are the "Earth grounding pad" of figure D-3. The guide's section 4.1 says the grounding lugs are M4 x 0.7 and are not supplied, so two common/ground-screw-m4@1 stand for the tapped holes; the library's two-hole lug pair is 5/8 inch (15.9 mm) and these measure 19.2, so the pair part is not used.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-sale notice for the 7280DR3A-36 (2026-10-22, a web search for "Arista 7280DR3A-36 end of sale announcement"): none found for this family. The notices that exist are for other 7280 models (the DCS-7280CR3K-36S, advisory 23790, and the older 7280QR-C36 and QR-C72), so the field reads none-announced.

line-system-ports.note: TWO OSFP CAGES at the upper right, "Line system port (OSFP)" 1 and 2 in the figure's callout table and "2 x OSFP-LS ports for dense 400G-ZR deployment" in the data sheet. A green strip under them prints "37" with an up triangle at its left end, LINE (read as LINE; the print is three pixels high) in the middle and "38" with an up triangle at its right: the two cages are numbered 37 and 38 as the fine print of the figure reads. Cage centres 307.7 and 337.9 mm from the left and 14.2 mm down, measured on the cage bezels (555 to 602 and 612 to 658 px, 118 to 145 px), a pitch of 30.2 mm. std/osfp@1 (23.1 x 13.5 mm) is seated; the figure draws the bezels 25 mm wide.

management-ports.note: A row of three at the right of the upper edge: console (callout 7, RJ-45 serial) at 381.7 mm, USB (callout 8, vertical, Type A) at 397.7 mm, Ethernet management (callout 9, RJ-45 with the two lamps drawn in its top corners) at 413.0 mm, all about 14.7 mm below the top. The guide's section 4.5 lists the cables: RJ-45 to DB-9 serial adapter and an RJ-45 Ethernet cable; the data sheet gives "RS-232 Serial Ports 1 (RJ-45)", "USB Ports 1" and "100/1000 Mgmt Ports 1" (as printed). The management jack is taken as 10/100/1000 (guide section 4.5: "Connect to 10/100/1000 management network") and so `1g`, where the data sheet's line reads "100/1000".

nameplate.note: A grey plate at the upper left, 32.1 x 11.3 mm, carries the maker's wordmark over the model line. The wordmark is not drawn; its box is the `logo-zone` region. The model line is plain text and is drawn: figure C-2 prints "7280DR3AM-36" because it is a picture of the DR3AM-36, the encryption variant of this chassis, and the guide's one figure serves the DR3A-36, the DR3AK-36 and the DR3AM-36. The line here reads 7280DR3A-36, the plate of the device this file is named for; the K and M variants print their own (see gaps).

numbering.note: THE NUMBERS ARE PRINTED TWICE ON THE FIGURE and the model follows the second. A white box with a large numeral sits over each cage in figure C-2, and the orange strip between the two rows prints a small `N-up-arrow` at its left end and `down-arrow-N+1` at its right, per column: 1 over 2, 3 over 4, ... 35 over 36. A seated cage hides anything painted under it, so the model prints the strip legends (which show in every render) and not the boxes. The strip legends were read on a eight-times enlargement of columns 1 to 4 (1 up, 2 down; 3, 4; 5, 6; 7, 8) and the callout 12 "Port numbers" of the guide covers both. Numbering starts at 1. The lower cage of each column is the even number, so the stack is column-major: port n is in column ceil(n/2), the upper row when n is odd. Interface names (Ethernet1 ... Ethernet36 and their breakouts) are EOS names and are not printed on the metal; they are not modelled.

port-lamps.note: ONE LAMP PER PORT, in the orange strip: the upper cage's lamp near the strip's top, about 4.3 mm left of the column centre, and the lower cage's near its bottom, 4.3 mm right of it (figure C-2, eight-times enlargement of columns 1 to 4; two green dots a pixel or two across per column). The guide's Appendix A.1.2 says port LEDs are "located in the vicinity of their corresponding ports" and table 10 gives the states: off link down, green link up, yellow software-disabled, flashing yellow failed diagnostics. The guide's figure A-3 is of another switch (the DCS-7050QX-32S) and shows four lamps a port; this face shows one.

port-wall.note: THIRTY-SIX QSFP-DD CAGES IN EIGHTEEN COLUMNS OF TWO. The white number boxes of figure C-2 were found as connected components (12 px, 6.4 mm, squares) and their centres fitted: column centres 39.0, 82.0, 125.0, 169.0, 212.0, 254.0, 298.0, 340.5, 384.0, 427.0, 471.0, 514.0, 557.0, 600.0, 643.0, 686.0, 730.0 and 773.0 px, a pitch of 43.18 px (734 px over 17 intervals) = 23.05 mm, the first at 19.75 mm ((39 - 2) / 1.873). The rows centre at 191.5 and 218.0 px, 46.2 and 60.3 mm below the top, a row pitch of 14.15 mm; 14.2 is used. The cages are std/qsfp-dd@1 (registry 19.0 x 10.0 mm); the figure draws them 20.6 wide with their bezel, which is the strip width below.

rear-layout.note: FIGURE D-3, the rear with a grounding point, 2RU: four fan modules left of the middle and two power supplies stacked at the right. The guide draws four generic rear panels (D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. D-1 and D-2 are 1RU. Of the 2RU pair, D-3 has an "Earth grounding pad" (callout 7) and D-4 has a plain separation between fans 1 and 2 with no ground. Table 6 of the guide says the DR3A-54 grounds with the KIT-GND-EXT-2RU side kit and the DR3A-36 "Attach directly - right angle lug recommended", the grounding location being "on the back for those supporting direct attach", so the DR3A-36 is mapped to D-3. THE MAPPING IS ESTIMATED: it follows from fan count (four), height (2RU), supply count (two) and table 6, not from a caption. The data sheet's rear thumbnail of the 7280R3A 2RU views shows the same four-fan, two-supply layout with a ground pad. MEASURED at 1.193 px/mm on the red fan frames: four modules 79.6 wide on 98.0, 85.5 and 85.5 mm steps (the first step spans the ground strip), x 5.9, 103.9, 189.4 and 274.9; supplies at x 361 (73.5 wide), top at 2.0 and 45.0 mm.

sources.note: 7280R3A Series Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, DOC-07042-01, 59 pages, PDF created 2025-05-16 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280R3A.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage environment), Table 3 (power input), Table 4 (power draw and supported supplies), Table 6 (grounding of the 2RU switches), section 2.1 (airflow orientation), sections 4.4 and 4.5 (power and serial cables), Appendix A (status indicators, figures A-1 and A-2, tables 9 to 13), Appendix B (parts list), Appendix C (front panel, figure C-2: DCS-7280DR3A-36, DCS-7280DR3AK-36 and DCS-7280DR3AM-36), Appendix D (rear panels, figures D-1 to D-4) and Appendix E (power supplies and fan modules, "all fans and power supplies are hot swappable"). 7280R3A Series Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 04-0040-26, 27 pages, dated April 15th, 2025 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7280R3A-Datasheet.pdf): the 7280DR3A-36 model comparison table, power supply specifications, ordering information and the platform overview. No 3D model, no CAD drawing, no studio photograph and no Visio stencil is held (intake SOURCES.md and COVERAGE.md read first); the data sheet's only picture of the face is a 400 px thumbnail, so figure C-2 is the instrument.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 18 QSFP-DD pairs (port-1/port-2 to port-35/port-36).

status-block.note: FOUR LAMPS beside the line-system ports, 4.8 mm apart at y 20.0 mm: system status, fan status, power supply 1 status and power supply 2 status (figure C-2 callouts 3 to 6; guide Appendix A.1.1, figures A-1 and A-2: "labeled either as in Figure A-1 or as in Figure A-2"). The two right-hand lamps are printed PS1 and PS2 and the two left-hand lamps carry a symbol (a circle with a mark, a fan) instead of a word. The symbols are not drawn: their strokes are two pixels wide and resolve to a blob (see gaps). States are table 9's: the system lamp blinking green (powering up), green, blue (beacon) or amber; the fan lamp green, amber or red; the supply lamps green or off.

timing.note: ToD AND TWO CLOCK CONNECTORS in the narrow strip at the right edge (callouts 10 and 11). The ToD connector is a vertical slot with a screw at each end; the data sheet's accessory "CAB-SYNCE-RJ  Spare Time of Day adapter cable (USB-C to 2 x RJ-45)" says its mate is USB-C, so std/usb-c@1 is turned a quarter at 429.3, 45.3 mm. Under it are two gold coax jacks, labelled PPS (upper) and 10MHz (lower) in the figure, at 59.3 and 67.1 mm. The data sheet's timing line reads "PTP and SyncE with OCXO and PPS/10M/ToD inputs". The coax type is not stated: std/smb@1 is seated because the jacks measure about 5.3 mm across their flange, which is nearer the SMB (4.83) than the SMA (6.35) in the registry, and the choice is estimated (see gaps).

vents.note: Two square-hole fields, each four rows deep, above and below the port wall (figure C-2: holes about 2.2 mm square on a 3.65 mm pitch, 6.85 px). Upper field y 25.1 to 38.4, lower y 67.8 to 81.2, both from x 5.9 to 423.3. The library's pattern for square openings is its grille tile, whose opening is 85 percent of the pitch where the hardware's is 60, so the holes read larger than the figure's, and four whole tiles need 14.6 mm where the figure's four holes span 13.3: the fields are drawn 14.6 tall (y 24.4 and 67.2) and 416.1 wide (114 tiles). A ribbed lip runs under the lower field (y 83.0 to 85.9).

weight.note: 24.1 kg (53.1 lbs) in the guide's Table 1; the data sheet's comparison table prints "53.1 lbs (24.09 kg)". The same figure to rounding; 24.1 is used.

references.title: 7280R3A Series Quick Start Guide (DOC-07042-01, PDF created 2025-05-16)

bottom.empty: Not drawn by either held document. The guide's section 4.2 names a grounding location on the bottom of the 1RU switches that take KIT-GND-EXT-1RU; table 6 puts the 2RU switches' on the side or the rear.

left.empty: Not drawn by either held document. Table 6 puts the KIT-GND-EXT-2RU attachment of the DR3A-54 on a side; the DR3A-36 attaches directly at the rear.

right.empty: Not drawn by either held document, and the guide's table 6 says nothing of the DR3A-36's side walls: the other side of the chassis, as the left.

top.empty: Not drawn by either held document. The guide's chapter 3 shows the chassis from above only in isometric drawings of a different switch (the DCS-7050QX-32S), and the data sheet shows no top view.
